samples.summary: `insertPlainText` still hits the `Doc.splitBlock` empty-list-item short-circuit that `insertBlocks` was just patched to avoid — and the diff makes that short-circuit convert the block to a heading
samples.evidence: The diff adds a workaround in `insertBlocks` (text-editor.ts:3610-3626) because `Doc.splitBlock` returns the *same* block id for an empty list item instead of splitting (document.ts:303-307). The sibling caller `insertPlainText` (packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:3536) was not updated: with the caret in an empty bullet, `docSplitBlock` returns the same id, the cursor is moved to offset 0 of that same block, and every subsequent line is prepended into one block — multi-line plain-text paste (Ctrl+Shift+V / `pastePlainTextFromClipboard`, text-editor.ts:3498-3510) collapses and reverses the lines. This change additionally makes that short-circuit convert an empty *bulleted heading* into a `heading` block (document.ts:301-307), so the same paste now also silently promotes the destination to Heading N. `ensureEditableBlock` (line 3520) is unaffected (hr/page-break only) and `editor.ts:3258/3277` are guarded by `offset > 0 && offset < len`.

samples.summary: The slides clipboard reaches the same docs `Block` model with no validation, bypassing the new `deserializeBlocks` sanitizer's threat model
samples.evidence: The diff hardens the docs internal clipboard because "any page can put [it] on the system clipboard" and unvalidated values flow "straight into the shared Yorkie tree, the renderer, and the DOCX/PDF exporters" (clipboard.ts:34-43). `packages/slides/src/view/editor/interactions/clipboard.ts:38-49` parses a JSON payload, checks only a `magic` string, and returns `parsed.elements as Element[]`; `Element` carries `blocks: Block[]` of the identical docs model (packages/slides/src/model/element.ts:1,265). It is reached from the paste handler at packages/slides/src/view/editor/interactions/keyboard.ts:819 and — worse — from `tryDeserialize` on the plain `text/plain` flavour at keyboard.ts:847, which any page can write. Those blocks are rendered by the shared docs text-box renderer and exported (PPTX/PDF), so the class of injection the diff closes for docs remains open one package over. Fix belongs on the slides deserializer (reuse a shared block sanitizer).

samples.summary: `sanitizeTableData` defaults a missing column width to `100`, but `TableData.columnWidths` are fractions of the table width everywhere else
samples.evidence: `for (let c = 0; c < cols; c++) columnWidths.push(asNumber(rawWidths[c]) ?? 100);` conflicts with the model contract established outside the diff: `createTableBlock` fills `Array(cols).fill(1 / cols)` (packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:542), the DOCX importer normalises to `w / totalWidth` (docx-importer.ts:277,484) and the exporter multiplies by the page width — `Math.round(w * totalTwips)` (docx-exporter.ts:232). A pasted table whose payload omits or corrupts `columnWidths` therefore gets columns 100× the table width in layout and ~900000 twips in the DOCX export instead of an even share. A safer default is `1 / cols`.

verdict.reason: Verified in the tree: Doc.splitBlock (model/document.ts:297-307) short-circuits on an empty list-item, calling setBlockType with unlistedBlockType(block) — which can be {type:'heading', headingLevel} (model/types.ts:337; test list-heading-roundtrip.test.ts:172) — and returns the SAME blockId. insertBlocks was explicitly patched to avoid this (text-editor.ts:3609-3627), but the sibling consumer insertPlainText calls docSplitBlock at text-editor.ts:3536 and then unconditionally moves the cursor to offset 0 of the returned id (3540), assuming a new block. docSplitBlock (403-407) is a thin wrapper and inherits the same-id return. No guard exists on that path: ensureEditableBlock (3516-3523) covers only horizontal-rule/page-break, and exitLinkIfAtTrailingEdge is unrelated. The path is reachable from Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+V (1054-1056 -> 3498-3510) and from the ordinary paste fall-through (1190-1192). The reviewer's impact narrative is overstated — the short-circuit can only fire while the block is still empty, i.e. when the pasted text starts with a newline, so one line is swallowed rather than all lines collapsing/reversing — but the presence claim is accurate: an unguarded consumer of the changed splitBlock contract that silently promotes the destination block to Heading N and drops a line. That is a changed-contract-with-unupdated-caller in this lens's lane, and overstated blast wording is not a refutation ground.

verdict.reason: Verified independently. packages/docs/src/view/clipboard.ts:22-30 and its threat-model comment at :36-43 add a rebuild-from-scratch sanitizer (sanitizeBlocks, :324-334) for clipboard-sourced Block[], explicitly because any page can write that payload and unvalidated values would flow into the shared Yorkie tree, renderer and exporters. packages/slides/src/view/editor/interactions/clipboard.ts:38-58 handles the same class of payload but checks only the magic string and Array.isArray, returning parsed.elements as Element[]; packages/slides/src/model/element.ts:1,265 confirms Element data carries blocks: Block[] of the identical docs model. Reachable: keyboard.ts:819 (custom MIME) and keyboard.ts:827/837 via tryDeserialize (keyboard.ts:845-851) on the text/plain flavour any page can write, then paste.ts:40-70 into store.addElement (memory.ts:558-594) which only clones the init and recomputes connector frames - no block validation. I searched wide for the supposedly missing sanitizer and found none: repo-wide grep for sanitiz/validate/zod/schema under packages/slides/src returns only OOXML namespaces and unrelated comments; every slides import from @wafflebase/docs is a type or DEFAULT_BLOCK_STYLE/generateBlockId/clearMeasureCache, never sanitizeBlocks/deserializeBlocks; all deserializeElements references are keyboard.ts plus a raw re-export at packages/slides/src/index.ts:228; the slides clipboard test only asserts the magic rejection. The slides editor is wired to a Yorkie-backed store (packages/frontend/src/app/slides/yorkie-slides-store.ts) and blocks reach the PPTX exporter (packages/slides/src/export/pptx/text.ts:1), so the path is live. In-lane for blast radius: a new guard whose protected operation is reached by an unguarded sibling entry point; major impact.
